boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments at Tulane’s Uptown and Downtown libraries, from quiet individual seating to reservable group rooms.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library, first floor
cards.notes: Set up at an individual or group work area, then use the available wireless, printers, power outlets, and assistive-technology workstation as needed.
cards.short_summary: Collaborative first-floor library space with research and technology support nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane describes the Learning Commons as a collaborative first-floor space with individual and group work areas, seating, wireless, printers, and power outlets.
cards.access_notes: Located in Howard-Tilton Memorial Library; consult the library’s current building-access policies before visiting.

cards.title: Second-Floor Study Commons
cards.subtitle: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library, second floor
cards.notes: Choose a carrel, larger workstation, or the standing-height countertop table; every workstation has power and the space has high-speed wireless.
cards.short_summary: Flexible second-floor seating for solo work or small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane states that the second-floor Study Commons has individual carrels, larger workstations, a standing countertop table, power at all workstations, and high-speed wireless.
cards.access_notes: Small-group and individual seating; no study spaces are reservable, according to Tulane Libraries.

cards.title: Selley Study Commons
cards.subtitle: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library, third floor
cards.notes: Use a carrel, pod workstation, or lounge seat with a tablet arm for individual work; keep calls, conversation, and group work elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: Designated quiet third-floor space for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane designates the third-floor Selley Study Commons as a quiet study area and says it has carrels, pod workstations, and individual lounge seating.
cards.source_title: Building Access & General Policies | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Cell phone use, talking, and group work are prohibited in this designated quiet-study area.

cards.title: Library Classroom 430
cards.subtitle: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check whether a class or event is scheduled; when the room is not in use, enter without a reservation and use one of its wooden tables.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor classroom that doubles as unscheduled study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane Libraries says Classroom 430 is open for student study without reservations when no library class or event is scheduled.
cards.source_title: New Library Classroom and Event Space Can Be Used for Studying Too | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available only when not scheduled for library-related classes or events; Tulane reports no reservation is needed for study use then.

cards.entity_name: Doris Z. Stone Latin American Library Open Stacks and Gallery Space
cards.title: Doris Stone LAL Open Stacks
cards.subtitle: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Take the elevator or stairs to the fourth-floor Latin American Library wing and use the open stacks and gallery area during Howard-Tilton opening hours.
cards.short_summary: Fourth-floor library gallery and stacks area with study access.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane states that the Doris Z. Stone Latin American Library’s open stacks and gallery space are accessible whenever Howard-Tilton Memorial Library is open.
cards.source_title: Visit Us | Doris Z. Stone Latin American Library and Research Center
cards.access_notes: Open stacks and gallery space follow Howard-Tilton Library hours; the special-collections reading room requires an appointment.

cards.title: Matas Group Study Room 2228
cards.subtitle: Rudolph Matas Library, second-floor Quiet Area
cards.notes: Reserve this 8–10-person room at least 24 hours ahead, or use it first-come if it is empty and has not been reserved.
cards.short_summary: Large second-floor health-sciences group room with study infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane lists Room 2228 as an 8–10-seat group study room in Matas Library’s second-floor Quiet Area, equipped with whiteboards, network connections, and power outlets.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces at Matas Library | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservations require 24 hours’ advance notice and may run up to six hours; empty unreserved rooms are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Matas Group Study Room 2230
cards.subtitle: Rudolph Matas Library, second-floor Quiet Area
cards.notes: Plan a larger project meeting here and reserve ahead through Matas; bring your materials for the room’s whiteboard, network, and power connections.
cards.short_summary: Large group room within the library’s glass-walled quiet area.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane identifies Room 2230 as an 8–10-seat Matas Library group study room in the second-floor Quiet Area with whiteboards, network connections, and power outlets.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces at Matas Library | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve at least 24 hours in advance; the room may be used first-come, first-served when empty and unreserved.

cards.title: Matas Mezzanine Room M201
cards.subtitle: Rudolph Matas Library, Mezzanine Level
cards.notes: Use this smaller room for an individual session or small project group; request it at least 24 hours in advance when you need a reservation.
cards.short_summary: Mezzanine group-study room sized for a compact working session.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane lists M201 as a 4–6-seat Matas Library group study room and states that single users may book mezzanine study rooms.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces at Matas Library | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Single users may book mezzanine rooms. Reservations need 24 hours’ notice and may run up to six hours.

cards.title: Matas Mezzanine Room M203
cards.subtitle: Rudolph Matas Library, Mezzanine Level
cards.notes: Reserve this 4–6-person mezzanine room for focused group work, and use its whiteboard, network connection, and power outlets to stay organized.
cards.short_summary: Small-group study room with whiteboard and connected work setup.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane lists M203 as a 4–6-seat Matas Library group study room; the library says its group rooms have whiteboards, network connections, power outlets, and seating.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces at Matas Library | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservations require 24 hours’ advance notice. If empty and unreserved, rooms are available first-come, first-served within posted limits.

cards.title: Matas Mezzanine Room M205
cards.subtitle: Rudolph Matas Library, Mezzanine Level
cards.notes: Book this 4–6-person room ahead for a shared work session, or check whether it is empty and unreserved for first-come use.
cards.short_summary: A compact mezzanine room for reserved or walk-in group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane lists M205 as a 4–6-seat Matas Library group study room and states that group rooms are first-come, first-served when empty and not reserved.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces at Matas Library | Tulane University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Matas at least 24 hours ahead; a reservation can be held for a maximum of six hours.
